messages:
liam: FYI — we need a scheduled rolling NIC firmware "warm-handshake" across az2 + az4 racks to fix the intermittent egress packet stalls we saw last week. Planning Tue Mar 10 02:00-06:00 UTC.

liam: Affected pools: gpu-pool-prod-az2 (primary), gpu-pool-batch-az4 (best-effort). Expected capacity hit per-cohort: ~5-12% while pods are being drained + prefix cache warming. Typical transient latency spikes 200-800ms for ~5-10s during NIC handoff.

anya: +1. Canary rack first? how many nodes per cohort?

liam: Canary = 8 nodes (one rack). After canary looks good wait 45m then continue in cohorts of 16 nodes (one or two racks depending on density). 30m gap between cohorts to watch telemetry.

maria: Any customers with pinned Dedicated during that window? We have one finance customer in az2 with SLA — flagged them via support already. If they want a blackout-free path we can schedule their instances on alternate pool pre-shift.

liam: Noted — thanks. We'll offer the dedicated migration + manual pin to alternate az if they request.

noah: Runbook sanity check: health checks to watch: 
- per-route 5xx rate > 0.5% rolling 5m 
- token-per-request latency p95 delta > +250ms 
- GPU utilization drop > 15% sustained after cohort start == backfill not happening

noah: Alert thresholds in pager duty: set staging threshold to 2x noisier so we don’t get paged for small blips during prefix warmup.

liam: Core steps (will copy to ops-runbook):
```
1) cordon nodes in cohort
2) kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
3) trigger BMC -> NIC warm-handshake script: /opt/fw/handshake.sh --hot-reboot
4) validate egress path: curl -H 'x-test: warm' https://health-check/egress?node=<node>
5) uncordon node
```

anya: Will we auto-scale other pools to replace capacity? We should avoid aggressive spot backfill that increases cost. Suggest temporary conservative autoscale: +10% max cpus for 1h per-cohort.

liam: Yes, conservative backfill only. Ops will set a transient policy: max_spot_burst = 10% and prefer reserved pools. Cost impact estimate: ~+$6k for window if we need sustained spot use to keep SLA.

maria: Ok — I'll prep customer comms and post to status.redwood with opt-out link.

deploy-bot: Calendar event created: "az2/az4 NIC warm-handshake maintenance" Tue Mar 10 02:00-06:00 UTC — invites sent to #eng-infra, #support, #sre-oncall.

noah: Monitoring checklist to attach to runbook: grafana dashboard link, example query for p95: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` and packet-drop query for NIC counters.

liam: If canary shows >3% error increase for 10m we abort and roll back NIC fw using hot-swap fallback. Rollback also if any customer P0 impacted.

anya: I'll be on-call for the canary + first two cohorts. liam, can you confirm you'll coordinate with oncall network eng for BMC access?

liam: Yep. I'll coordinate with neteng and keep this thread updated with cohort start timestamps and post mortem notes. :thumbsup:

maria: Posting customer note now. Also tagging legal for compliance sign-off (will attach fw vendor cert).

deploy-bot: Reminder set: 1h before window
